pages.title: Public journalism
pages.summary: A journalism reform movement associated with Jay Rosen that argues journalists should help public life work, not only observe it from a distance.

body.heading: Why it matters here
body.text: This concept is a key path into the archive because it connects Rosen's scholarship, teaching, and public criticism across decades. The wiki should use it as an example of a page that explains an idea while linking readers back to primary archive records.

body.heading: Editorial stance
body.text: Wiki prose should summarize what archive records and reliable sources say. It should not settle scholarly disputes, publish new interpretations, or turn community notes into unsourced claims.

references.label: Issue 499: Community wiki for archive records, concepts and entities

pages.title: Jay Rosen
pages.summary: Jay Rosen is the central subject of the archive: a journalism professor, critic, author, and public thinker whose work spans press criticism, public journalism, blogging, social media, and the press-public relationship.

body.heading: Role in the archive
body.text: Entity pages should help readers move from a name to the records, concepts, publications, and debates connected to that name. For the launch scaffold, this page demonstrates entity structure without enabling public edits yet.

pages.title: Press-public relationship
pages.summary: A recurring frame for understanding how journalism imagines, addresses, serves, ignores, or learns from the public.

body.heading: Use as a bridge page
body.text: This page should become a bridge between dissertation material, archive records, and entity pages. It is also a good candidate for stricter sourcing rules because it is interpretive and central to the collection.

pages.title: Audience relationship
pages.summary: A recurring question in the archive about how journalism understands the people it addresses, serves, ignores, measures, or invites into public work.
aliases: People formerly known as the audience

body.heading: Why this page exists
body.text: This concept page gives the wiki a place to connect archive records about audiences, publics, participation, blogging, and social media without flattening those ideas into a single tag. Future record links should be curated from source records rather than inferred from keyword matches alone.
